measurement_notes: Unmeasured job peaks remain null until a completed gate records a representative output size; unknown is not a reservation. Estimates for GCC Debug/Release, ASan/UBSan, and Icarus are exact-SHA observed output-tree sizes and are not filesystem high-water measurements.

Icarus, GCC Debug/Release, ASan/UBSan, and the Verilator combined source/build plus installed-prefix tree cap use twice their respective measured output-tree sizes so accumulated smaller files also trigger review. A hosted v5.052 installed prefix measured 257,576,704 bytes across 127 files on commit ae0dbd016ed32abfcaec24351e0679f3b892f3db, with a 231,709,824-byte debug executable. On commit d9e118d99d4b213c87a71bc6dd40b61cf61453c7, the aggregate Verilator scan measured 2,236,212,581 regular-file bytes across 11,201 files in .tools/verilator and the installed prefix; one redirected entry was skipped. This post-build output-tree observation sets the 4,472,425,162-byte aggregate cap but does not measure filesystem high-water or complete-build peak, which remains unknown. The operation-specific 256 MiB per-file cap accommodates the observed compiler executable.
The developer profile warns below 50 GiB and blocks below a 40 GiB reserve; these are configurable workstation safeguards, not architecture limits.
The hosted profile retains the existing 2 GiB free-space floor and is independent of developer-workstation thresholds.
